*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph --improve` on 2026-05-20. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/ralph-pipeline-08-crews/plan.md`.*

**Worktree:** `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan` creates the worktree at `D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.ralph\jobs\ralph-pipeline-08-crews\worktree\` on branch `ralph-pipeline-08-crews`. All file edits happen in that worktree; commits land on the branch and are merged to `main` after Phase 6 review converges. Do NOT edit `main` directly.

**Note:** This plan reads from `.crews/` (shared workspace state, not branch state). The cross-walk MUST resolve `.crews/` from the main repo root, never from a worktree-local directory. See Risk Area 4 below.

## Overview

The user runs an overview-bookkeeping agent (lead role in the crews plugin) that delegates phase work to crew members spawned via `/spawn-member`. The overview needs to track which crew member's session worked on each phase of each task — enabling continuity (lead resumes the same member), audit (trace decisions back to a transcript), and parallelism (lead spawns multiple members across tasks).

The crews plugin runtime state lives under the consuming workspace's `.crews/` directory. Each member's `manifest.json` exposes the canonical `sessionId` and `transcriptPath` we need. Plan 08 adds a `CrewSessionRef[]` per `RalphStage` to `RalphPipelineState`, populated from two complementary paths: (a) a heuristic cross-walk that runs on every watcher tick, and (b) explicit subcommand writes from `/work-on --via-crew`. Conflict resolution and persistence are designed so explicit entries survive across ticks unchanged.

PowerShell single-quote escaping uses `''`.

### Technical Constraints
- **Lock contract.** Watcher holds the lock for its lifetime. Subcommands MUST fail fast against a running watcher with the canonical `another sync in progress …` diagnostic — they do NOT queue. `/work-on --via-crew` is expected to be invoked when `pnpm overview` watcher is stopped (one-shot sync between phases) or via the operator's lead-orchestration discipline. A future queue/IPC layer is out of scope for Plan 08 and tracked in the Open Questions section.
- **Path safety on Windows.** `path.startsWith` is unsafe for the cwd filter (`D:\repo2` startsWith `D:\repo`). Use `path.relative(repoRoot, manifestCwd)` and accept the manifest when the result is `''` (exact repo root) OR is relative, non-absolute, and not prefixed with `..`. Case-normalize both sides (`.toLowerCase()`) before comparison.
- **Substring collision.** Plain `lastSummary.includes(taskId)` matches `overview-viewer` inside `overview-viewer-polish`. Use a custom-boundary regex (see Approach below). When multiple task IDs match, log to stderr and pick the LONGEST (most specific) match.
- **`additionalProperties: false` config schema.** `.ralph/overview-config.schema.json` rejects unknown fields. Adding `crewsRoot` requires schema + `default-config.mjs` + `default-config.d.mts` + `resolve-config.mjs` updates atomically.
- **Worktree-aware `.crews/` root.** Plan 08 implementation runs from a linked worktree, so the default `.crews` path must NOT be resolved against the worktree's `repoRoot`. `resolve-config.mjs` detects worktree mode with `git -C <repoRoot> rev-parse --git-dir` and `git -C <repoRoot> rev-parse --git-common-dir`; when those differ, relative `crewsRoot` values resolve against `path.resolve(repoRoot, commonDir, '..')`, making the default `.crews` path the main repo's `.crews/`. Watcher, subcommands, and cross-walk receive this single resolved `config.crewsRoot`.
- **Spawn-member runtime contract.** The crews plugin's `/spawn-member` slash command only triggers the spawn side-effect when invoked from a user prompt. Invoking it via the `Skill` tool from another skill does NOT fire the hook. `/work-on --via-crew` MUST use the CLI mirror at `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/spawn-member.js`.
- **Manifest field race.** Right after `/spawn-member` returns, the new member's `manifest.json` may not yet have `sessionId` / `transcriptPath` populated — those are written by Claude's SessionStart hook, which races with spawn. `/work-on --via-crew` polls the manifest for up to 10s (500ms interval). If still empty, record the partial entry keyed by `(crewName, memberName)` (plus cwd, startedAt) and let the next heuristic tick fill in `sessionId` / `transcriptPath` in place.

## Approach

### Architecture

Plan 08 adds two independent paths into `RalphPipelineState.crewSessions`:

1. **Heuristic cross-walk** — `discoverCrewSessions({ repoRoot, ralphState, overviewData, crewsRoot, now, logger })` runs in `sync-core.mjs` on every full walk and every incremental merge. It walks `.crews/crews/*/members/*/manifest.json` + `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/manifest.json`, filters by `cwd ⊆ repoRoot`, and matches members to tasks via task-ID-in-`lastSummary` (strong signal) or task-ID-in-spawn-launcher-prompt (medium signal). For each matched `taskId`, it reads the stage from `ralphState.byTaskId[taskId].stage` at discovery time and inserts the session into that `RalphStage` bucket. If the task later advances to a different stage, existing entries remain under their recorded stage and are NOT migrated. Returns a sparse `Map<taskId, Record<RalphStage, CrewSessionRef[]>>`.
2. **Explicit writes** — `scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs` gains `--update-crew-session <taskId> <stage> --json <ref>` and `--finalize-crew-session <taskId> <stage> --member <name> --outcome <s> [--summary <text>]`. Both share the watcher's lock and fail fast if held.

**Persistence of explicit-ness.** `CrewSessionRef` gains serialized `crewName`, `memberName`, and `_isExplicit?: boolean` fields. Explicit subcommand writes set `_isExplicit` to `true`. Heuristic discovery omits `_isExplicit`. Merge identity is `sessionId` when present, otherwise fallback `(crewName, memberName)`; if a heuristic discovery has a `sessionId` and matches a partial explicit entry by `(crewName, memberName)`, upgrade that explicit entry in place by filling missing `sessionId`, `transcriptPath`, and `startedAt` in the entry's existing stage bucket. Merge rule (on every tick): if an existing entry for the same identity exists in any stage bucket, preserve that recorded stage bucket rather than relocating it to the task's current stage; if the existing entry has `_isExplicit === true`, also preserve its `endedAt` / `outcome` / `summary` and do NOT overwrite them with heuristic-derived values. Explicit subcommand writes always win and update the entry in place.

**Stale-member detection.** Inside `discoverCrewSessions`: if `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` is older than 60 minutes AND the existing entry has no `outcome`, set `outcome: 'stopped'` + `endedAt: lastHeartbeatAt`. Idempotency guard: if the existing entry already has `outcome` set (any value), preserve it across ticks — do NOT re-derive.

**Watcher integration.** Extend `getWatchRoots()` to additionally include `path.join(crewsRoot, 'crews')` and `path.join(crewsRoot, 'sessions-configs')`. In `parseWatchedPath()`, detect paths under those two `.crews/` roots BEFORE the existing Ralph `rootEntries` loop and return `{ kind: 'crews' }` with no slug. In `flushPending()`, branch on `kind === 'crews'` before calling `deriveAffectedTaskUpdate()`; crew changes invoke a new `rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite({ currentState, config, repoRoot, overviewData })` helper instead of per-slug Ralph derivation. If a debounce batch contains both Ralph and crew changes, apply the normal Ralph `mergeAndWrite()` first, then run the crew rescan against the resulting state. `scheduleFlush()`'s existing 2s debounce already coalesces; reuse it. Excluded patterns (`.crews/logs/**`, `.crews/spawn-launchers/**`, `.crews/crews/*/members/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/members/*/outbox.jsonl`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/outbox.jsonl`, `.crews/crews/*/inbox-history.jsonl`) MUST be added to `default-config.mjs` ignored list — the manifest is the canonical state source.

**Conflict survival across ticks.** Because `walkRalphState()` rebuilds from `.ralph/` and does NOT carry forward prior state, the explicit-vs-heuristic merge runs WITHIN a tick using the prior snapshot's `crewSessions` (loaded from `plans/overview-snapshot.json` at the start of the tick) as the authoritative explicit set. The full walk path reads the prior snapshot before invoking `discoverCrewSessions`, then merges heuristic discoveries on top, preserving entries where `_isExplicit === true`.

### Implementation Strategy

1. **Story 1 — Add types.** `CrewSessionRef` interface + `RalphPipelineState.crewSessions` field in `tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts`. `CrewSessionRef` includes `crewName`, `memberName`, optional `sessionId`/`transcriptPath` for partial entries, and serialized `_isExplicit?: boolean`. Typecheck both `tools/overview-viewer/` and root scripts.
2. **Story 2 — Config plumbing.** Add `crewsRoot` to `default-config.mjs`, `default-config.d.mts`, `resolve-config.mjs`, and `.ralph/overview-config.schema.json` as a top-level schema `properties.crewsRoot: { "type": "string" }` entry. In `scripts/lib/default-config.d.mts`, add required top-level `crewsRoot: string` to the `RalphOverviewConfig` interface (required because `default-config.mjs` supplies a default). Default config value: `.crews`. In `watcher.ignored`, add `.crews/crews/*/members/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/members/*/outbox.jsonl`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/outbox.jsonl`, and `.crews/crews/*/inbox-history.jsonl` alongside the existing `.crews/logs/**` and `.crews/spawn-launchers/**` exclusions. In `resolveConfigPaths()`, include `crewsRoot` in the known root destructuring and return `crewsRoot: resolveCrewsRoot(repoRoot, config.crewsRoot)` so the field is not dropped. `resolveCrewsRoot()` resolves absolute overrides unchanged; for relative values, it first computes the main repo root by comparing `git -C <repoRoot> rev-parse --git-dir` with `git -C <repoRoot> rev-parse --git-common-dir`. If those differ, the base is `path.resolve(repoRoot, commonDir, '..')`; otherwise the base is `repoRoot`. This makes the default `.crews` resolve to the main repo's `.crews/` even when the process runs inside `.ralph/jobs/ralph-pipeline-08-crews/worktree/`. Add resolver tests for both a config override and linked-worktree mode.
3. **Story 3 — Spawn-launcher parser.** `scripts/lib/parse-spawn-launcher.mjs` exports `parseSpawnLauncher(absolutePath) -> { initialPrompt: string | null, memberName: string | null, crewName: string | null }`. Handles PowerShell single-quote escaping (`''` → `'`), extracts last single-quoted argument from the `claude ...` line. Test against real spawn-launchers and synthetic edge cases.
4. **Story 4 — Crew cross-walk.** `scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs` exports `discoverCrewSessions(opts) -> Map<taskId, Record<RalphStage, CrewSessionRef[]>>`. Walks `.crews/crews/*/members/*/manifest.json` and `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/manifest.json`, filters by cwd, matches by task ID (custom-boundary regex), reads the stage from `ralphState.byTaskId[taskId].stage`, dedupes by `sessionId` and exposes `(crewName, memberName)` so sync-core can merge later heuristic data into partial entries without `sessionId`, marks stale entries, logs unmatched/ambiguous to stderr. Tests cover positive match, stage bucketing from `ralphState`, cwd filter including `cwd === repoRoot` acceptance, multi-task ambiguity, stale detection, missing-manifest tolerance.
5. **Story 5 — Wire into sync-core.** `mergeAndWrite()` and `assembleStateFromBundles()` invoke `discoverCrewSessions` AFTER per-slug Ralph-side derivation. Both paths load the prior snapshot's `crewSessions` and apply the `_isExplicit` preservation rule using the shared identity function (`sessionId` first, fallback `(crewName, memberName)`) across all stage buckets. Export `rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite({ currentState, config, repoRoot, overviewData })`, which re-runs `discoverCrewSessions`, merges the result into `currentState.byTaskId[*].crewSessions` while preserving existing entries in their recorded stage buckets, preserving existing `_isExplicit` entries, upgrades partial explicit entries in place when heuristic data supplies `sessionId`/`transcriptPath`, updates only crew-session data / generated timestamp, and calls `writeSidecar()` without re-reading or re-deriving Ralph bundles. Tests cover: heuristic adds new entries, explicit entries from prior snapshot survive intact, an entry recorded under `stage='implementing'` stays there after the task advances to `stage='reviewing'`, stale-flag is set, idempotency on repeated ticks, crew-only rescan leaves non-crew Ralph fields unchanged.
6. **Story 6 — Extend watcher.** `getWatchRoots()` adds `<crewsRoot>/crews/` and `<crewsRoot>/sessions-configs/`. `parseWatchedPath()` checks these roots before the Ralph `rootEntries` loop and returns `{ kind: 'crews' }` with no slug. The flush handler partitions crew changes from Ralph changes, never passes `kind: 'crews'` to `deriveAffectedTaskUpdate()`, and invokes `rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite()` for any crew change after any normal Ralph `mergeAndWrite()` in the same debounce batch. Tests cover: `.crews/` mailbox file change is ignored, `.crews/crews/*/members/*/manifest.json` change triggers a flush, debounce coalesces multiple `.crews/` events, and a crew-only flush does not call `deriveAffectedTaskUpdate()`.
7. **Story 7 — Subcommand modes.** `scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs` accepts `--update-crew-session <taskId> <stage> --json <ref-json>` and `--finalize-crew-session <taskId> <stage> --member <name> --outcome <s> [--summary <text>]`. Both: parse args → acquire lock (fail fast on contention with canonical diagnostic) → load the current Ralph sidecar from `config.outputs.sidecarJson` (`plans/overview-ralph-state.json`), NOT the derived snapshot at `config.outputs.snapshot` (`plans/overview-snapshot.json`) → apply mutation to `state.byTaskId[taskId].crewSessions[stage]` using `sessionId` or fallback `(crewName, memberName)` identity (set `_isExplicit: true` for both) → call `writeSidecar()` → release lock. `writeSidecar()` receives the sidecar-shaped state (`generatedAt`, `generatedFromCommit`, `byTaskId`, `unmatched`) and regenerates `overview-snapshot.json` downstream. Example: `--update-crew-session foo implementing --json '{"crewName":"ralph-pipeline","memberName":"alice","sessionId":"s1"}'` reads `plans/overview-ralph-state.json`, upserts `byTaskId.foo.crewSessions.implementing[]`, then `writeSidecar()` emits both the updated sidecar and derived snapshot. Tests cover: serialized invocations succeed; concurrent invocation against a watcher-held lock fails before write with canonical diagnostic; finalize updates an existing entry's `endedAt`/`outcome`/`summary` in place.
8. **Story 8 — `/work-on --via-crew` branch.** Replace the Plan 06 placeholder in `.claude/skills/work-on/SKILL.md` with the actual flow: (a) derive next command via `derive-next-command.mjs`; (b) generate a unique member name (slug from task ID + short timestamp); (c) invoke `node D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/spawn-member.js <name> --crew <crewName> --cwd <repo_root> -- "<derived-command-prompt>"`; (d) poll `.crews/crews/<crewName>/members/<name>/manifest.json` for up to 10s at 500ms intervals waiting for `sessionId` and `transcriptPath`; (e) call `node scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs --update-crew-session <taskId> <stage> --json <CrewSessionRef>` with at least `crewName`, `memberName`, `cwd`, and `startedAt` even if `sessionId` / `transcriptPath` are still absent; (f) return to the bookkeeping agent. Document the fail-fast behavior when the watcher owns the lock.
9. **Story 9 — Tooltip extras.** Extend `RalphTooltipExtras` in `TaskCommand.tsx` to render crew session rows for the current `stage`. Each row shows: member name, `startedAt` → `endedAt || 'live'`, outcome (or "live" if undefined), and a clickable `file://` link to `transcriptPath` (re-write Windows backslashes to forward slashes for the URL). Use existing `.tooltip-extras-row` styling.
10. **Story 10 — Stale-flag idempotency tests.** Synthesize a manifest with `lastHeartbeatAt` 2h ago, run two consecutive `discoverCrewSessions` calls, assert the `endedAt` does NOT change between calls. Then synthesize a member that briefly revives (touches heartbeat) and assert the existing `outcome: 'stopped'` is preserved.
11. **Story 11 — Conflict-resolution tests.** Write an explicit entry via subcommand; then trigger a heuristic walk that would also discover the same `sessionId`. Assert the explicit `summary` / `outcome` / `endedAt` survive intact. Add the partial-entry race case: write an explicit entry with `crewName`/`memberName` but no `sessionId`, then trigger a heuristic walk for the same member with `sessionId`/`transcriptPath`; assert the original entry is upgraded in place rather than duplicated.
12. **Story 12 — Cascade audit + INDEX refresh.** Atomically update `plans/ralph-pipeline-INDEX.md` (Source-of-truth modules table, DAG dependency for Plan 09), any related plan documents that reference `RalphPipelineState` fields or sync-core extension points, and `scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.test.mjs` with an explicit Ajv regression for the new `crewSessions` contract. Include each diff in the final commit message.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `CrewSessionRef` type with serialized `crewName`, `memberName`, and `_isExplicit?: boolean` fields; `RalphPipelineState.crewSessions?` map. `sessionId` / `transcriptPath` are optional until the manifest race resolves.
- Heuristic cross-walk of `.crews/crews/*/members/*/manifest.json` and `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/manifest.json`. Match by task ID in `lastSummary` (strong) or in spawn-launcher prompt (medium). Cwd filter via `path.relative`. Dedupe by `sessionId`, falling back to `(crewName, memberName)` for partial entries.
- Watcher additions: `.crews/crews/`, `.crews/sessions-configs/` as new roots; `crews` event kind triggers full crew-rescan; existing 2s debounce reused. Mailbox/outbox files are excluded via explicit `.crews/crews/*/members/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/members/*/outbox.jsonl`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/outbox.jsonl`, and `.crews/crews/*/inbox-history.jsonl` patterns in `default-config.mjs`, alongside logs/spawn-launchers.
- Config plumbing for `crewsRoot` (default `.crews`, resolved to the main repo root's `.crews/` when `repoRoot` is a linked worktree).
- `--update-crew-session` and `--finalize-crew-session` subcommands on `scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs`. Share `sync-lock.mjs` with the watcher; fail fast on contention with canonical diagnostic.
- `/work-on --via-crew <crewName>` branch: spawn via crews CLI mirror, poll manifest, record `CrewSessionRef` via subcommand.
- Stale-member detection (`lastHeartbeatAt > 60min` → `outcome: 'stopped'`), idempotent across ticks.
- Conflict resolution via serialized `_isExplicit` flag: explicit entries survive tick boundaries; heuristic discoveries fill in missing entries but never overwrite explicit `endedAt`/`outcome`/`summary`. If a partial explicit entry has no `sessionId`, a later heuristic discovery for the same `(crewName, memberName)` upgrades it in place with `sessionId`, `transcriptPath`, and `startedAt`.
- Tooltip extras rows for crew sessions on the current stage (member, time range, outcome, `file://` transcript link).
- Tests for heuristic match (positive + negative + cwd filter + ambiguity), subcommand-mode lock contention (no-watcher + watcher-running), stale idempotency, conflict resolution across ticks, `/work-on --via-crew` end-to-end (mocked spawn), tooltip render.
- Cascade audit refresh of `plans/ralph-pipeline-INDEX.md`.

### Out of Scope
- MCP tools `overview.list_crew_sessions` and `overview.get_transcript` (Plan 09 wraps this data in MCP tools).
- Multi-crew coordination across multiple lead agents (single-lead model only).
- Queue/IPC layer that would let subcommands coexist with a running watcher. Subcommands fail fast on contention; the operator's discipline is to stop the watcher before invoking `/work-on --via-crew` (or invoke between watcher ticks while the watcher is intentionally stopped). Tracked as Open Question OQ-1.
- Live (non-snapshot) member status; the snapshot's `CrewSessionRef` reflects state as of the last tick. Real-time status reads `manifest.json` directly (Plan 09's MCP layer).
- Worktree-local `.crews/` directories. Watch root is the main repo's `.crews/` only.

## Risk Areas

1. **Lock contention with running watcher.** Subcommands cannot coexist with the long-lived watcher lock. Mitigation: fail fast with canonical diagnostic, document operator workflow. Re-evaluate in Plan 09 if friction observed.
2. **`_source` persistence gap (now resolved).** `_isExplicit` is serialized, so explicit entries survive across ticks and are distinguishable from heuristic discoveries. Test coverage in Story 11 enforces this.
3. **Substring collisions on task IDs (now resolved).** Custom-boundary regex (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])<id>(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])`) avoids `overview-viewer` matching `overview-viewer-polish`. Longest-match tiebreaker when multiple IDs match.
4. **Worktree-local `.crews/` shadow.** Plan resolves `.crews/` from the main repo root via `crewsRoot` config. `resolveConfigPaths()` must detect linked worktrees by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; when they differ, the default relative `.crews` is resolved from `path.resolve(repoRoot, commonDir, '..')`, not from the worktree path. `/implement-with-ralph` worktree at `.ralph/jobs/ralph-pipeline-08-crews/worktree/` must NOT introduce its own `.crews/` (verify by walking only resolved `config.crewsRoot`).
5. **Manifest-field race after spawn.** `/work-on --via-crew` polls for `sessionId`/`transcriptPath` with a 10s timeout. On timeout, records the partial entry keyed by `(crewName, memberName)`; next heuristic tick fills in the rest in place instead of creating a duplicate. Document this in the SKILL.md.
6. **Path-safety on Windows.** Cwd filter uses `path.relative` + case-normalization, not `startsWith`. Accept `path.relative(repoRoot, manifestCwd) === ''` as the exact repo-root case. Test against `D:\repo` vs `D:\repo2` to confirm the prefix attack fails.
7. **Spawn-member runtime contract.** `/work-on --via-crew` uses the crews CLI mirror, NOT the Skill tool — the slash command's hook side-effect doesn't fire through Skill invocations. Document this in SKILL.md.
8. **Schema strictness.** `.ralph/overview-config.schema.json` rejects unknown properties. `crewsRoot` is added atomically across schema + default-config + resolve-config + d.mts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CrewSessionRef` interface (with serialized `crewName`, `memberName`, optional `sessionId`/`transcriptPath` for partial entries, and `_isExplicit?: boolean`) and `RalphPipelineState.crewSessions?: Record<RalphStage, CrewSessionRef[]>` added to `tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts`.
- [ ] `crewsRoot` config field added to `default-config.mjs`, `default-config.d.mts`, `resolve-config.mjs`, and `.ralph/overview-config.schema.json` top-level `properties` as `{ "type": "string" }`. Default config value `.crews`. `resolveConfigPaths()` explicitly returns `crewsRoot: resolveCrewsRoot(repoRoot, config.crewsRoot)`, preserving absolute overrides and resolving relative values against the main repo root when `repoRoot` is a linked worktree (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` differs from `--git-dir`). Validated via schema validation, a resolver test that loads a `crewsRoot` override and asserts an absolute resolved path, a linked-worktree resolver test that asserts default `.crews` resolves to the common repo root's `.crews/` rather than the worktree's `.crews/`, and `pnpm sync-ralph-state` accepting a config override that sets `crewsRoot`.
- [ ] `scripts/lib/parse-spawn-launcher.mjs` extracts the initial prompt from a real spawn-launcher PS1 file (the final single-quoted argument on the `claude ...` line, with PowerShell `''` escape handling).
- [ ] `scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs` walks `.crews/crews/*/members/*/manifest.json` + `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/manifest.json`, applies the cwd filter via `path.relative` while accepting the exact `cwd === repoRoot` case, matches task IDs via custom-boundary regex, dedupes by `sessionId`, and emits `crewName`/`memberName` for fallback merging of partial entries. Stderr-logs unmatched and ambiguous matches.
- [ ] Watcher includes `<crewsRoot>/crews/` and `<crewsRoot>/sessions-configs/` in `getWatchRoots()`. `parseWatchedPath()` detects those roots before the Ralph `rootEntries` loop and returns `{ kind: 'crews' }` with no slug. Mailbox/outbox files excluded via `.crews/crews/*/members/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/members/*/outbox.jsonl`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/mailbox.json`, `.crews/crews/*/leads/*/outbox.jsonl`, and `.crews/crews/*/inbox-history.jsonl` ignore patterns in `default-config.mjs`, alongside log/spawn-launcher exclusions.
- [ ] Crew watcher events are handled by `rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite()` and are never passed to `deriveAffectedTaskUpdate()`. A crew-only flush re-runs `discoverCrewSessions`, preserves `_isExplicit` entries, writes the sidecar, and does not re-read or re-derive Ralph bundles.
- [ ] `pnpm sync-ralph-state --update-crew-session <id> <stage> --json <ref>` loads `config.outputs.sidecarJson` (`plans/overview-ralph-state.json`), atomically upserts a session entry under `byTaskId[id].crewSessions[stage]` with `_isExplicit: true` using `sessionId` or fallback `(crewName, memberName)`, calls `writeSidecar()` with the sidecar-shaped state, and survives subsequent heuristic ticks.
- [ ] `pnpm sync-ralph-state --finalize-crew-session <id> <stage> --member <m> --outcome completed --summary <text>` loads `config.outputs.sidecarJson` (`plans/overview-ralph-state.json`), atomically updates the matching sidecar entry's `endedAt`, `outcome`, `summary` in place, and calls `writeSidecar()` with the sidecar-shaped state.
- [ ] Both subcommands fail fast with the canonical `another sync in progress (pid <N>, process <label>, started <ts>)` diagnostic when the watcher owns the lock; no partial snapshot write occurs in this case.
- [ ] `/work-on --via-crew <crewName>` spawns a member via `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/spawn-member.js`, polls the manifest for `sessionId`/`transcriptPath` with a 10s timeout, records the session ref via `--update-crew-session` with fallback `crewName`/`memberName` identity when manifest fields are absent, and returns control to the lead.
- [ ] Tooltip extras render crew session rows with member name, time range, outcome, and clickable `file://` link to `transcriptPath` (Windows backslashes converted to forward slashes).
- [ ] Stale-member detection: a member with `manifest.lastHeartbeatAt` >60min old gets `outcome: 'stopped'` + `endedAt: lastHeartbeatAt` on the next tick. Idempotent: re-running the tick does NOT shift `endedAt`.
- [ ] Conflict resolution: explicit entries with `_isExplicit: true` survive a subsequent heuristic walk that would otherwise re-derive the same `sessionId`. Explicit `summary` / `outcome` / `endedAt` are preserved exactly. Partial explicit entries with no `sessionId` are matched by `(crewName, memberName)` and upgraded in place when the heuristic walk later discovers `sessionId` / `transcriptPath`; no duplicate entry is created. Existing entries are matched across all `RalphStage` buckets and remain in their recorded bucket; a session first recorded under `implementing` is not migrated or duplicated when the task later advances to `reviewing`.
- [ ] All existing tests pass (root `pnpm test`, `tools/overview-viewer` vitest split projects, typecheck across packages).
- [ ] Cascade audit applied atomically in the final implementation commit: `plans/ralph-pipeline-INDEX.md` Source-of-truth modules table and DAG, `tools/overview-viewer/README.md` (if it lists `RalphPipelineState` fields), `scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.mjs` (explicit `crewSessions` schema), and `scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.test.mjs` with an Ajv positive case for a valid `crewSessions` array plus a negative case for a malformed `CrewSessionRef` missing required `memberName`. Commit message lists each diff for reviewer verification.

## Open Questions

- **OQ-1:** Should a future plan add a queue/IPC layer to let `--update-crew-session` subcommands coexist with a running watcher? Plan 08 explicitly fails fast; the operator's discipline is to stop `pnpm overview` before invoking `/work-on --via-crew`. If lead agents in practice need to record sessions while the watcher is running, this becomes a friction point. Deferred to Plan 09 evaluation.
- **OQ-2:** Should `discoverCrewSessions` cap the number of crew sessions retained per `(taskId, stage)` to avoid unbounded growth across many spawns? Plan 08 leaves the list unbounded; if production data shows >50 entries per stage, add a most-recent-N cap.
- **OQ-3:** The custom-boundary regex (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])<id>(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])`) assumes ASCII task IDs. If task IDs ever contain unicode characters, revisit. Current task IDs (verified in `plans/overview-data.js`) are all ASCII kebab-case.
